applies_why: The judge text addresses whether witnesses pressed against the D2 vs C3 link count as unanswered toward a broken link, so it applies K-G4's subject.
quote: the line is cured by retraction, not defended: every witness pressed against C3 was named and answered in the challenger's own later rounds ((DR2) §C and (DR3) C3 quoting Matthew 1:18, 1:25 and Deuteronomy 22:24; (DR3) C4 quoting Luke 1:34), so the "witness left unanswered" ground fails and the collision is regraded UNDERDETERMINED; with that retraction the challenger's standing is corrected to SELF-SUPPORTED (L=6, c=0, no link BROKEN)
rule_words: A verse on a side's 'cited in' line counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count. A verse the judge counts toward a broken link is counted this way. If the judge says a verse was answered, the judge must not count it. Not counting it obeys this rule.
room: If the judge says a verse was answered, the judge must not count it. Not counting it obeys this rule — whether a judge who says answered must still supply a pressed/retracted line, or whether saying answered and not counting is enough; I read it as the latter because the rule says not counting obeys.
why: The judge says the witnesses were answered in later rounds and treats them as not counting toward a broken link, which is what K-G4 permits and requires once answered.
